full_judgment:
M. Enayetur Rahim, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings against the accused-petitioners contained in Special Case No.12 of 2011 corresponding to Metro Special Case No. 128/2010 arising out of Uttara Police Station case No. 36 dated 21.06.2000 under Sections 406/409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 now pending in the Court of Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders should not be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 1. Brigediar Mohammed Ali Hassan 2. Lieutenant Colonel Anowaruzzaman 3. Mejor A.B.M. Nesar Uddin in respect of 08(eight) Projects under Bangladesh National Cadet Core (BNCC) applied for allotment of 3200 Metric tons wheat to the Secretary Ministry of Durjak Babostapona and Tran by letter dated 26.08.1997. And accordingly 1500 Metric tons wheat were allotted vide memo dated 13.11.1997. Thereafter, on behalf of the Director, BNCC, the Deputy Director sent a letter dated 16.11.1997 to the Director General, Food Directorate requesting to withdraw the said allotment of wheat from Narayangonj Silo instead of local Godown of Savar and the Food Directorate approved the said prayer and informed the same to District Food Controller, Narayangonj. In the meantime the accused petitioners with preplanned agreed to sale the allotted goods to the wheat businessman accused Md. Riazul Huq Chowdhury of Narayogonj at price of Tk. 5.00 per Kg, which was total valued at Tk.75 lacs and the accused Md. Riazul Huq Chowdhury paid .the said amount of TK.75 lacs by D.D. No.1028183/10 dated 24.11.1997 and the same was deposited in the Bank account of the Director BNCC and on the other hand an illegal authority was given by the BNCC under the signature of the accused Lt. Colonel Anwaruzzaman to accused Md. Riazul Huq Chowdhury to withdraw the alleged goods from the Narayangonj Food Godown and also to sale the same and thereafter, Riazul Huq Chowdhury withdrew the said goods from Narayangonj Food Godown as per D.O. No. 2810519 dated 09.12.1997 issued by the District Food Controller, Narayongonj. The said wheat was neither taken in the project area nor had any work been done; but the accused persons sold out the wheat with ill motive in open market. The sale of that wheat was illegal as per 'Village Structural Reform Policy and Circular; moreover, at that time the price of wheat was Taka 11.64 per Kg but the accused sold it as Taka 5.00 per Kg, and in this way the total Government price was Taka 1,74,60,000/- of 1500 Metric tons wheat but they sold it at price of Tk. 75,00,000/- and thereby they misappropriated Tk.99,66,000/- and thus, committed offence under sections 406/409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the prevention of corruption Act 1976. On the basis of said FIR Uttara Police Station Case No.36 dated 21.06.2000 under Sections 406/409/109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1974 was started against the 04(four) accused petitioners. 

 3. The case being ready for trial, the case record was transmitted to the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka and the case was registered as Metro. Special Case No.128 of 2010 and again the case record was transmitted to the learned Special Judge No.3 Dhaka for trial and the case was then renumbered as Special Case No.12 of 2011. 

 10. Mr. Shah Md. Zahurul Haque, the learned Advocate, appearing for the opposite party no. 2 Anti-Corruption Commission submits that the Commission after holding proper investigation submitted charge-sheet against the present petitioners having found prima facie case of misappropriation and misconduct within the mischief of sections 406/409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the prevention of corruption Act, 1947 and accordingly, charge was framed against the accused petitioners and as such there is no scope to quash the proceeding at this stage. Mr. Haque further submits that the accused petitioners never faced 'Court Martial' for the offence in question which is a civil offence and thereby, subsequent trial by Criminal Court for same offence is not barred under any provision of Army Act, 1952 and as such there is no merit of alleged departmental inquiry (Court of inquiry), if any at all, and as such the plea of double jeopardy is not applicable in this particular case. 

 11. Mr. Hoque having placed relevant file of the Commission relating to the present case submits that 'Sena Sadar (Army Head Quarter)' has failed to provide any documents/papers relating to the alleged proceeding of Court of inquiry, its decisions and recommendations to the Commission, as required by it and the 'Sena Sadar' informed the Commission that no such documents/papers kept in its office. Thus, the submissions of the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners regarding assembling of Court of inquiry have got no basis. 

 22. The learned Advocate for the accused petitioner having referred to paragraph 8 of the application has tried to convince us that, a Court of inquiry was assembled relating to the present allegation and it made some recommendation after holding inquiry. But the learned Advocate for the Commission has placed the relevant file of the case keeping with the Commission. It appears from that file that Commission by its letter dated 26.01.2010 addressed to the Adjutent General of Bangladesh Army, Sena Sadar, Dhaka requested to provide the relevant documents, recommendation of Court of inquiry regarding the present allegation.  26. Section 90 of the Army Act 1952 prohibits of second trial only in case of acquittal or conviction.
